road.title: It's not just a stay. It's part of the ride.
road.lede: Because every road deserves a great place to end. Five things decide whether a long day on a bike finishes well — and they are the five things we check before a property ever goes on this site.

pillars.title: Rider-friendly
pillars.body: Not a badge we hand out. A stay earns it by having what a rider actually needs at the end of the day — and every one of those answers is printed on the listing.

pillars.title: Late check-in
pillars.body: Ghats close, weather turns, days run long. Someone is awake and the gate opens when you finally roll in — no argument at a reception desk at one in the morning.

pillars.title: Secure parking
pillars.body: Covered, off the road, inside the gate. On the coast, a freshwater tap too, so the salt comes off before it starts eating the chrome.

pillars.title: Rider support
pillars.body: Chain lube, a foot pump and the spanners you forgot. Drying space for gear that met the monsoon. And the number of a mechanic who is genuinely open.

pillars.title: Great riding routes
pillars.body: Every stay lists the roads around it, with distances and an honest note on what the surface is really like — written by people who rode it, not scraped off a map.

riderFriendly.title: What rider-friendly means here
riderFriendly.lede: Secure parking, late check-in, bike facilities and roads worth the detour. It is not a badge we hand out — a stay earns it by having the things that decide whether a long day on a bike ends well.
riderFriendly.body: Most listing sites will tell you a place is good for bikers. Almost none of them will tell you whether there is a roof over the parking, whether the gate is manned at midnight, or whether there is a tap you can rinse the salt off with before it eats the chrome. Those are the questions we ask before a property goes on this site, and the answers are printed on every listing.

riderPassport.title: Rider Passport
riderPassport.lede: Keep a record of every StaySutra stay, route and ride.
riderPassport.body:
Most trips leave nothing behind but a bank statement. The Rider Passport is the other record — where you stayed, what you rode to get there, and in what order. It is stamped at every StaySutra property, it travels with you between trips, and it is yours to keep.

We are building it now. Join the list and you will be among the first to carry one — and you will hear about new properties and new routes before they reach the site.

howItWorks.title: Join the list
howItWorks.body: A name and a mobile number. That is the whole form, and it is the only thing we will ever ask you for.

howItWorks.title: Stay with us
howItWorks.body: Every StaySutra booking becomes an entry — the property, the destination and the date.

howItWorks.title: Log the ride
howItWorks.body: The road in gets recorded alongside the stay, so the passport reads as a route rather than a receipt.

howItWorks.title: Carry it forward
howItWorks.body: First look at new properties and routes, and recognition at every stay in the network.

about.title: Where stays meet stories
about.lede: StaySutra is a curated stay network built on one idea: that where you sleep is part of the journey, not an afterthought at the end of it. Riders taught us that first.

listProperty.title: Turn your property into a stay people remember.
listProperty.lede: Hand us the whole job — photography, listing, pricing, marketing and every guest message. Four steps, about ten minutes. We review every submission ourselves and come back to you within two working days.

steps.title: Tell us about the property
steps.body: Who you are, where it is, and what kind of place it is.

steps.title: What it offers
steps.body: Capacity, amenities and — the part that matters here — what you have for the bikes.

steps.title: Photos and documents
steps.body: Pictures of the place, plus proof you are entitled to list it.

steps.title: Review and submit
steps.body: Check it over, agree to the terms, and send it to us.
